\chapter{Secondary Structure Probability}
\label{\detokenize{SecondaryStructure:secondary-structure-probability}}\label{\detokenize{SecondaryStructure::doc}}

\section{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{SecondaryStructure:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{DynamiSpectra} provides a comprehensive secondary structure analysis tool for molecular dynamics simulations based on .dat files. This module calculates the frame\sphinxhyphen{}wise probability of each structural state—such as α\sphinxhyphen{}helices, β\sphinxhyphen{}sheets, loops, turns, bends, and 3\sphinxhyphen{}helices—across simulation replicas. The results are visualized using boxplots, allowing for comparative analysis of secondary structure stability and population among different simulation groups.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{ss\PYGZus{}analysis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}folder}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{simulation\PYGZus{}files\PYGZus{}groups}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{plot\PYGZus{}config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{SS}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guidence:} This graph shows the probability distribution of each secondary structure type across the simulation. Variations in these probabilities can reflect structural stability or conformational changes over time. Consistent probabilities suggest stable elements, while shifts may indicate unfolding or rearrangements.

\chapter{Secondary Structure Fraction}
\label{\detokenize{FractionSS:secondary-structure-fraction}}\label{\detokenize{FractionSS::doc}}

\section{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{FractionSS:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{DynamiSpectra} provides a comprehensive secondary structure analysis module tailored for molecular dynamics simulations. This module processes simulation data to quantify the fraction of each secondary structure type—such as α\sphinxhyphen{}helices, β\sphinxhyphen{}sheets, and loops—across all trajectory frames. The resulting time\sphinxhyphen{}resolved plots enable detailed visualization of secondary structure composition dynamics throughout the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Command line in GROMACS to generate .xvg files for the analysis:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
gmx\PYG{+w}{ }dssp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}s\PYG{+w}{ }Simulation.tpr\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}f\PYG{+w}{ }Simulation.xtc\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}o\PYG{+w}{ }ss.dat
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{fractions\PYGZus{}ss\PYGZus{}analysis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{file\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}folder}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{plot\PYGZus{}config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{FSS}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guidance:} The presented graph illustrates the temporal evolution of the fractions of residues adopting different secondary structure elements. Monitoring these fluctuations facilitates assessment of structural stability and conformational dynamics within the system. Consistent patterns may indicate stable folding, while variations can reveal conformational transitions or local instabilities. Comparative analysis across simulations aids in identifying reproducibility and the effects of differing initial conditions or parameters. Observed changes often correspond to the formation or disruption of critical structural motifs, thereby providing valuable insights into the molecular behavior under investigation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Note:} The .dat file contains raw data from the molecular dynamics simulation, classifying the secondary structure of each protein residue across all frames. The code reads this file and, for each frame, counts residues in each secondary structure type (e.g., α\sphinxhyphen{}helices, β\sphinxhyphen{}sheets, loops). It then calculates the fraction of each structure by dividing the count by the total number of residues. These fractions are plotted over time, showing how secondary structure proportions evolve during the simulation.

\chapter{System Pressure}
\label{\detokenize{Pressure:system-pressure}}\label{\detokenize{Pressure::doc}}

\section{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{Pressure:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{DynamiSpectra} provides an analytical tool to evaluate pressure profiles across molecular dynamics simulations using .xvg files. The module calculates the mean pressure from multiple replicates and displays a time series plot with the standard deviation as a shaded region, helping to assess stability and fluctuations over time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to ensemble analysis, \sphinxstyleemphasis{DynamiSpectra} supports individual plots for each replicate and generates kernel density plots to visualize the distribution of pressure values. These outputs offer insight into system equilibrium, variability between replicates, and potential instabilities during the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Command line in GROMACS to generate .xvg files for the analysis:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
gmx\PYG{+w}{ }energy\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}f\PYG{+w}{ }Simulation.edr\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}o\PYG{+w}{ }pressure\PYGZus{}simulation.xvg
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{pressure\PYGZus{}analysis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}folder}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{simulation\PYGZus{}file\PYGZus{}groups}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{pressure\PYGZus{}config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{density\PYGZus{}config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{Pressure}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guidance:} The resulting plots illustrate the temporal evolution of system pressure. A stable pressure profile over time suggests that the system has reached equilibrium and is maintaining consistent thermodynamic conditions. In contrast, large fluctuations or drifts may indicate issues with system stability, improper equilibration, or external perturbations influencing the simulation dynamics.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{plot\PYGZus{}pressure\PYGZus{}density}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{results}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}folder}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[width=500\sphinxpxdimen]{{Pressure_density}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guidance:} This plot represents the pressure distribution derived from the temporal profile of system pressure. Peaks in the distribution indicate frequently sampled pressure values, reflecting the most common thermodynamic states of the system. Broader peaks suggest greater variability or fluctuations in pressure, while sharper, well\sphinxhyphen{}defined peaks indicate stable and consistent pressure throughout the simulation.

\chapter{System Temperature}
\label{\detokenize{Temperature:system-temperature}}\label{\detokenize{Temperature::doc}}

\section{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{Temperature:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{DynamiSpectra} offers a dedicated module for analyzing system temperature across molecular dynamics simulations using .xvg files. This module computes the mean temperature from multiple replicates and presents a time\sphinxhyphen{}series plot with the standard deviation as a shaded region, enabling assessment of temperature stability and fluctuations throughout the simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alongside the time\sphinxhyphen{}resolved analysis, DynamiSpectra also generates kernel density plots to depict the overall temperature distribution. These outputs help identify equilibration status, detect anomalies across replicates, and verify the maintenance of target temperatures under simulation conditions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Command line in GROMACS to generate .xvg files for the analysis:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
gmx\PYG{+w}{ }energy\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}f\PYG{+w}{ }Simulation.edr\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}o\PYG{+w}{ }Termperature\PYGZus{}simulation.xvg
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{temperature\PYGZus{}analysis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}folder}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{simulation\PYGZus{}file\PYGZus{}groups}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{temp\PYGZus{}config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{density\PYGZus{}config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{Temperature}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guidance:} The resulting plots show the temporal evolution of system temperature. A stable temperature profile indicates proper equilibration and control of the simulation ensemble. Significant fluctuations or trends may suggest insufficient thermal coupling, poor equilibration, or external perturbations affecting thermal stability.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[width=500\sphinxpxdimen]{{temperature_density}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guidance:} This plot represents the distribution of temperature values throughout the simulation. Sharp, narrow peaks indicate stable and consistent thermal behavior, while broader peaks suggest greater variability or temperature fluctuations. Comparing distributions across simulations can help identify differences in thermal stability or ensemble control.

\PYG{l+s+sd}{Processes multiple groups of temperature replicates, calculates mean and std, and plots results.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{Parameters:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZhy{} output\PYGZus{}folder: str, directory to save plots}

                \PYG{k}{raise} \PYG{n+ne}{ValueError}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Error reading file: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
            \PYG{n}{times}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{times}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{mean\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{std\PYGZus{}temp}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\chapter{System Density}
\label{\detokenize{Density:system-density}}\label{\detokenize{Density::doc}}

\section{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{Density:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{DynamiSpectra} offers a comprehensive analytical framework to evaluate the density distribution within molecular systems during molecular dynamics simulations, utilizing input data in .xvg file format. This analysis enables detailed insights into the spatial arrangement and concentration of particles in the system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The software’s graphical interface allows users to visualize the average density profiles derived from multiple simulation replicates, with the corresponding standard deviation depicted as a shaded region to represent variability. Additionally, \sphinxstyleemphasis{DynamiSpectra} supports the analysis of individual simulation replicas, enabling plots to be generated from single datasets when multiple replicates are not available or not required.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guidance:} The resulting plots illustrate the temporal evolution of system density. A consistent profile indicates stable particle distribution throughout the simulation, while significant fluctuations may reflect structural rearrangements, phase transitions, or other dynamic processes affecting system compactness or organization of the system.

\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guidance:} This plot represents the density distribution derived from the temporal profile of system density. Peaks in the distribution indicate regions of higher particle concentration within the system. Broader peaks suggest a more heterogeneous or variable distribution, whereas sharper, well\sphinxhyphen{}defined peaks correspond to stable and consistent density regions throughout the simulation.

\chapter{Contributing}
\label{\detokenize{Contributing:contributing}}\label{\detokenize{Contributing::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Contributions are welcome, and they are greatly appreciated! Every
little bit helps, and credit will always be given.


\section{Bug reports}
\label{\detokenize{Contributing:bug-reports}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxhref{https://github.com/Conradoou/DynamiSpectra/issues}{reporting a bug} please include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Your operating system name and version.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any details about your local setup that might be helpful in troubleshooting.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detailed steps to reproduce the bug.

\end{itemize}


\section{Documentation improvements}
\label{\detokenize{Contributing:documentation-improvements}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
DynamiSpectra could always use more documentation, whether as part of the
official DynamiSpectra docs, in docstrings, or even on the web in blog posts,
articles, and such.


\section{Feature requests and feedback}
\label{\detokenize{Contributing:feature-requests-and-feedback}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The best way to send feedback is to file an issue at \sphinxurl{https://github.com/Conradoou/DynamiSpectra/issues}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are proposing a feature:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Explain in detail how it would work.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep the scope as narrow as possible, to make it easier to implement.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Remember that this is a volunteer\sphinxhyphen{}driven project, and that code contributions are welcome.

\end{itemize}
